Document 242
Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume
                    E–7, Documents on South Asia, 1969–1972
242. Transcript of Telephone Conversation Between Secretary of State
Rogers
and the
                            President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (
Kissinger
)
1
2
Washington
,
March 29, 1972, 11:30 a.m.
R: The Pakistan minister you are going to see later today?
K: I don’t know what about.
R: He is going to give you a hard sell on renewing supply of military
                            equipment to Pakistan.
K: That’s not on.
R: He said they have to have arms to negotiate with India. He will give
                            you the hard sell. I told him this was a Presidential decision and under
                            the circumstances it was tough for us to consider such a program. I
                            think encouragement would be harmful.
K: I won’t give him any. I have serious doubts that even the President,
                            who is very pro-Pakistan is even thinking about it.
[Omitted here is discussion unrelated to South Asia.]
